newsitem.title: JAPAN: Shares in some regional Japan banks extend losses.
newsitem.headline: Shares in some regional Japan banks extend losses.

text.p: Shares in some regional banks continued to slide on Wednesday morning, as worries about their financial health lingered after Hanwa Bank Ltd was ordered to halt most of its business earlier this month.
Shares in Fukutoku Bank, based in western Japan, fell 18 yen to 222 yen by 0128 GMT on the Osaka Securities Exchange on volume of 375,000 shares. The share price has dropped for six days.
Tokuyo City Bank Ltd, based in Sendai, slipped 31 yen to 160 yen by 0128 GMT, making it the largest percentage loser in the first section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
Tokuyo City Bank shares were depressed partly by selling related to the expiry of six-month margin transactions, traders said.
On the other hand, shares in Hanshin Bank Ltd were up eight yen to 358 yen by 0200 GMT on the OSE. Volume was 644,000 shares.
